title: Long-Term Legibility of Static Files: Plain-Text Preservation
subtitle: Why dependence on runtime layers and proprietary databases leads to irreversible digital asset decay
audience: Keynote for Open Source Architecture Conference & Async Engineering Review

slides.title: Long-Term Legibility of Static Files: Plain-Text Preservation
Structured data trapped in dynamic databases becomes unrecoverable once runtime environments vanish
items: Over 68% of legacy CMS databases cannot export raw semantic content after server shutdown
Proprietary codecs and binary serialization lose maintainers and execution runtimes within 5 to 10 years
Raw data lacking self-contained styling and semantics reduces to fragmented bytes
slides.cap: Source: Digital Preservation Foundation 2025 Software Archeology Survey Report

slides.title: Self-contained HTML encapsulation guarantees precise rendering across standard browsers for decades
items: Packaging CSS variables and font bases into a single file eliminates external CDN link breakdown risks
Standard HTML5 semantic tags provide enduring structured markup for future text parsers
Zero runtime dependencies ensure assets can be previewed and printed directly from any file system
slides.cap: Intersection of physical print and web standards: Treating web pages as digital printed artifacts

slides.title: Legibility depends not on modern authoring tech, but on human readability without tools thirty years later
Adopt a static-first distribution pipeline to permanently decouple enduring assets from ephemeral tooling
items: Bind textual content directly with visual presentation for archiving
